summary: Unscoped session propagation prevents temporary RBAC grants for internal tools
description:
Issue summary:
Temporary role grants issued via the internal 'just-in-time' (JIT) approval flow are not being applied consistently to interactive console sessions. Affected users receive the approval confirmation but continue to see 403s when accessing the target app until they perform a full re-login.

Impact:
- Multiple engineers and on-call rotation members are unable to assume temporary elevated roles for runbook access and debugging tools without a full sign-out/sign-in.
- Productivity impact for incident response: estimated 30-45 minutes per affected person to recover.

Environment:
- prod-us-east identity-proxy + auth-service behind the LB
- Okta Identity Provider recently migrated to new SAML->OIDC bridge (rolled 2026-03-08)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger JIT approval for a temporary role via the internal console (requestor flow).
2) Approver approves the request; approval shows success in UI.
3) Requestor clicks 'assume role' from confirmation modal.
4) Requestor receives 200 on the approval endpoint but subsequent calls to the console API return 403 until the user signs out and signs back in.

Observed behavior:
- Approval endpoint returns success and audit logs show temporary role grant recorded in the RBAC service.
- Identity-proxy session cookie does not appear to include the newly granted role claim for the current session.
- Full sign-out/sign-in refreshes session cookie with correct role claim and access is restored.

Expected behavior:
- The JIT approval flow should attach the temporary grant to the current session (via session propagation or re-issue) so that no explicit sign-out is required.

Notes:
- This started after the IdP migration; hypothesis is that the new bridge changes the session scoping or token exchange semantics which the identity-proxy code does not handle for in-flight session re-issuance.

investigation_notes: Audit entry AUD-77422 shows RBAC service applied temp grant at 2026-03-10T09:10:21Z for user riley.GrantId=G-9932.

Identity-proxy logs (proxy-01) around 2026-03-10T09:10 show: 'session_refresh: no reissue_needed=false, incoming_token_scopes=[openid email], outgoing_cookie_claims=[sub,email]'. Missing 'roles' claim on outgoing cookie.

Okta OIDC bridge token introspection returns role claim present in access token post-grant, but identity-proxy is reading only id_token scopes and not merging access_token claims for the current session.
Reproduced in staging by forcing grant flow; adding a manual session re-issue endpoint call populates roles into the cookie and access is restored immediately.

Hypothesis: the IdP migration changed which token (id_token vs access_token) carries transient role attributes. identity-proxy currently trusts id_token for session claims and ignores access_token claim merges.
Risk assessment: P1 until patch deployed in prod-us-east. Workaround available (session re-issue) but is manual. No evidence of role elevation persistence beyond intended TTL.

resolution:
Workaround: admins can trigger a session re-issue via the admin tool to immediately apply temporary grants for affected users. Communication posted to #oncall and affected teams.

Plan: identity-proxy patch to merge access_token transient claims (roles) into the session cookie on JIT grant path. Candidate patch authored and under review in PR 458. Canary deploy scheduled to prod-us-east with feature flag 2026-03-12 11:00.

Follow-ups: 1) Add automated integration test that asserts role propagation without full sign-out after JIT grant. 2) Update runbook to include session re-issue short-term step. 3) Postmortem entry and timeline if patch rollout impacts users.
